resources.string: Blocks Reels, Shorts and TikTok — in the apps and in the browser

ShortBlock reads the screen content of Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and your browser only, in order to detect Reels, Shorts and algorithmic feeds and navigate away from them. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere — the app has no internet permission.
ShortBlock works through an accessibility service. Three steps, in this order — step 2 stays greyed out until step 1 is done.

Android 13 and newer block accessibility for sideloaded apps. In the app info screen tap the ⋮ menu at the top right and choose “Allow restricted settings”. If that entry is missing, this step is already done.

Under “Installed apps” / “Downloaded apps” pick ShortBlock and switch it on. Also switch on the shortcut (“Accessibility button”) — that floating button at the edge of the screen is what redeems the daily cheat. It no longer turns ShortBlock on and off; that is done here in the settings.

Recommended on Xiaomi, Samsung and OnePlus devices — they stop background services aggressively. On Xiaomi/HyperOS also allow “Autostart” in the app info and lock the app in the recents view; otherwise the system switches the accessibility service off again after a reboot or overnight.
Service is off — nothing is being blocked
Closes the Reels viewer — from the tab, Explore, a DM or the browser. Stories stay untouched.
Instagram: block the For You feed
Forces the chronological “Following” feed and stops at the end of it, before the suggested posts start.
Closes the Shorts player, the Shorts tab and youtube.com/shorts in the browser. Normal videos, search and subscriptions keep working.
Service is running · last event %1$s ago
Service is running · nothing seen for a while
Android reports the service as on, but it is not running in this process. Switch the accessibility service off and on again — and turn on the two options below so it stops happening.
Shows a permanent silent notification. Costs a notification, but stops the manufacturer from killing the service after a few hours.
No internet permission, no analytics, nothing leaves the device.
Forces the Following tab. DMs, search and profiles keep working.
Every attempt to open TikTok navigates straight back — app and tiktok.com in the browser. With an allowance the chosen minutes a day stay open.
Please switch to “Following” at the top
If the app closed something it should not have: this is the rule that fired. Report the line and it can be narrowed down.
Android has disabled the accessibility service — nothing is being blocked. Tap to switch it back on.
A reel or short someone sends you plays once, all the way. The swipe to the next one blocks. From the Reels or Shorts tab everything stays closed.
Today\'s 5 minutes are still free — the button at the edge of the screen.
%1$d min left. Then it closes again.
After that it closes again — and there is no second one today.
Free again tomorrow. Until then the answer is no.
You can switch it back on in ShortBlock — if you really want to.
Press the accessibility button at the edge of the screen — deliberately, not from the app. That short detour is the whole point.
Nothing is being blocked right now.
Once a day, %1$d minutes of everything — triggered by the accessibility button at the edge of the screen.

resources.string: When Instagram or YouTube change their layout, blocking silently stops working. Turn this on, open the screen that is no longer blocked, come back here and copy the matching IDs into Rules.kt.

While recording is on, the service listens to every app — that is how you find out the real package name if a blocker never fires. It only ever blocks the apps it is configured for.
